pencereler.0-5: A Boeing 707 ran out of fuel and crashed on a Long Island hillside.
pencereler.5-12: It broke apart, and seventy three people were killed. The flight was held in three holding patterns. Fuel ran
pencereler.12-20: low. The crew asked for priority, but never said emergency. After a missed approach, the engines flamed out. Controllers didn't grasp how
pencereler.20-30: little fuel was left. Fuel emergency terms were standardized.

segmentler.metin: Avianca Flight 052 ran out of fuel and crashed on Long Island.
It took only a crew that never declared a fuel emergency.
So how could a crew that never declared a fuel emergency do this?
The answer is holding delays and a missed approach while controllers didn't understand the fuel state — and it is why fuel emergency terminology was standardized.
